gloss: sorry to keep you waiting; thanks for waiting

definitions.gloss: sorry to keep you waiting; thanks for waiting
definitions.explanation: A set phrase used when arriving late or when someone has been waiting for you. Also used by service staff when bringing food or completing a task.

examples.japanese: お{待|ま}たせ！⟦{遅|おく}れて→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧ごめん。
examples.english: Sorry for the wait! Sorry I'm late.

examples.japanese: お{待|ま}たせ⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧。ご⟦{注文|ちゅうもん}→注文：03485_chuumon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{品|しな}→品：03192_shina⟧です。
examples.english: Thank you for waiting. Here is your order.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧お{待|ま}たせ⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。⟦ただいま→ただいま：01062_tadaima⟧お⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ご⟦{案内|あんない}→案内：01291_annai⟧⟦いたします→いたす：01314_itasu⟧。
examples.english: I'm very sorry to have kept you waiting. I will show you to your seat now.

notes:
Shortened form of お{待|ま}たせ⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧. The casual form お{待|ま}たせ is used between friends and family, while お{待|ま}たせ⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧ is standard polite, and ⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧お{待|ま}たせ⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧ is humble/formal.

POLITENESS LEVELS:
- お{待|ま}たせ: casual, among friends
- お{待|ま}たせ⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧: standard polite, used in shops and restaurants
- ⟦{大変|たいへん}→大変：00594_taihen⟧お{待|ま}たせ⟦いたしました→いたす：01314_itasu⟧: very formal, used in business or upscale service

USAGE:
Used in two main contexts:
- When you arrive and someone has been waiting for you
- When service staff deliver something to a customer (food, documents, etc.)

The phrase is almost automatic in service contexts. Even if the wait was very short, staff will say お{待|ま}たせ⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧ as a courtesy.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{遅|おく}れて→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧すみません: sorry for being late — a direct apology for lateness, not used in service contexts
- お⟦{待|ま}ち→待つ：00469_matsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧: please wait — the requesting side, not the apologizing side
